page.overview:
What is Spidops?

Spidops evolves from Tarountula starting at level 15.

Spidops may have been inspired by the Ogre-faced spider or related members of the Deinopidae family (also known as net-casting spiders), who are known to hold their legs together in pairs and cast nets. Its segmented wooden-like body and association with strings may derive cues from marionettes. Its behaviour calls in mind special operation forces, especially its pop culture depiction of secret agents, with its eyes resembling night-vision goggles and chest plating resembling a bulletproof vest, a typical outift for special ops forces. The ability to hang upside-down using its thread evokes the trope of secret agents using cables to hang from ceilings, popularized by the Mission Impossible series of movies, although some real-life spiders showcases this behaviour as well.

Alternatively, it could be based on the yokai Tsuchigumo, who were said to have the face of an oni and the body of a spider. They are known to disguise themselves and capture travelers with its strings, most famously portrayed in the stories, The Tale of the Heike and Tsuchigumo Sōshi.

Spidops may be a combination of spider, spy, ops (abbreviation of "operations"), and Deinopis (genus of the ogre-faced spider).
